creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Cacio e Pepe
description: Four ingredients and no room to hide. The sauce is made from pasta water and cheese, off the heat, or it splits.
steps: Bring a shallow pan of well-salted water to the boil — use less water than usual so it ends up starchy.
Toast the cracked pepper in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute, until it smells sharp.
Cook the pasta 1 minute short of the packet time, then lift it into the pepper pan with a cup of the water reserved.
Take the pan off the heat and let it stop sizzling, about 30 seconds. This is the step that decides whether the sauce works.
Add the pecorino with a splash of pasta water and toss hard until it turns glossy, adding water a spoonful at a time.
Serve at once, with more pepper.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Chicken Katsu Curry
description: Crisp panko cutlets over a dark, faintly sweet curry sauce. The sauce is better made a day ahead.
steps: Soften the onion and carrot in oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the curry powder and garam masala and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the stock, honey and soy, bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes, until the carrot is soft.
Blend the sauce smooth and keep it warm. It should coat a spoon; loosen with water if not.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Shallow-fry in 1cm of oil over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until deep gold and cooked through — no pink at the thickest point.
Rest on a rack for 2 minutes, slice, and serve over rice with the sauce poured alongside.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Pork Carnitas Tacos
description: Shoulder cooked slowly in its own fat until it shreds, then crisped under the grill. Worth the afternoon.
steps: Heat the oven to 150C.
Season the pork all over with the salt, cumin and oregano.
Put it in a heavy casserole with the onion, garlic and the squeezed orange halves, and add water to come a third of the way up.
Cover and cook for 3 hours, until the meat gives completely to a fork.
Shred the pork coarsely and discard the aromatics. Keep the fat and juices.
Spread the meat on a tray, spoon over some of the fat, and grill on high for 5 minutes until the edges crisp.
Pile into warm tortillas with raw onion and coriander.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Chana Masala
description: A weeknight chickpea curry that gets its depth from cooking the onions properly and finishing with amchur.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 12 minutes, stirring, until genuinely golden — this is most of the flavour.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, coriander and turmeric and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes, until the oil separates at the edges.
Add the chickpeas and a splash of water, and simmer for 12 minutes.
Crush a few chickpeas against the side to thicken the sauce.
Finish off the heat with the garam masala and amchur, and season.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
description: Fry the paste in coconut cream until it splits and smells of nothing else. That step is the whole dish.
steps: Spoon the thick cream from the top of one can into a wide pan and heat it over medium-high.
Add the curry paste and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until the oil separates and the paste darkens.
Add the chicken and turn it in the paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, add the aubergine and lime leaves, and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the aubergine is soft.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar — it should taste salty, sweet and hot in that order.
Stir through the basil off the heat and scatter with chilli.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Bún Chả
description: Grilled pork patties dropped into a sweet-sour dipping broth, with cold noodles and a pile of herbs.
steps: Mix the pork with the garlic, shallot, 1 tbsp fish sauce and 2 tsp sugar. Rest it for 20 minutes.
Whisk the broth: 4 tbsp fish sauce, the vinegar, 3 tbsp sugar and the warm water. Add the shaved carrot and set aside.
Shape the pork into small flat patties, about 4cm across.
Grill over high heat for 3 minutes a side, until charred at the edges and cooked all the way through.
Drop the hot patties straight into bowls of the dipping broth.
Serve with the cold noodles and the herbs, dipping as you go.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Kimchi Jjigae
description: The stew you make when the kimchi has gone too sour to eat straight. Sourer is better here.
steps: Render the pork belly in a dry pot over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, until the fat runs and the edges brown.
Add the kimchi and fry it in the fat for 5 minutes — do not skip this, raw kimchi tastes thin in the finished stew.
Stir in the gochujang, gochugaru and sugar.
Add the kimchi juice and the water, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes.
Slide in the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes more without stirring, so it stays whole.
Finish with the sesame oil and spring onions.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Mapo Tofu
description: Numbing, hot, and on the table in twenty minutes. The Sichuan pepper goes in at the end, ground fresh.
ingredients: or omit for a vegetarian version
steps: Slide the tofu into barely simmering salted water and leave it while you cook — it firms up and seasons through.
Fry the pork in the oil over high heat for 3 minutes, until it is no longer pink and starting to crisp.
Turn the heat to medium, add the doubanjiang and fry for 1 minute, until the oil turns red.
Add the black beans and garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer.
Drain the tofu and add it, then push it gently with the back of a spoon rather than stirring.
Add the cornflour slurry and simmer for 1 minute, until it thickens and clings.
Off the heat, scatter over the ground Sichuan pepper and the spring onions.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Coq au Vin
description: A braise that rewards browning properly and then leaving it alone. Better reheated the next day.
steps: Heat the oven to 160C.
Render the lardons in a heavy casserole over medium heat for 6 minutes, then lift them out.
Brown the chicken in the fat, skin side down first, for 5 minutes a side. Do it in batches — crowding steams it.
Set the chicken aside and brown the shallots and mushrooms in the same pot for 6 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, scraping the bottom, and let it bubble for 3 minutes.
Return the chicken and lardons, add the stock, thyme and bay, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook in the oven for 90 minutes, until the meat pulls from the bone.
Lift the chicken out, reduce the sauce on the hob until it coats a spoon, and whisk in the butter off the heat.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Lamb Souvlaki with Tzatziki
description: Marinate the day before if you can. The yoghurt in the marinade does more than the lemon.
steps: Mix the lamb with the half cup of yoghurt, garlic, lemon zest, oregano and oil. Chill for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Make the tzatziki: stir the grated cucumber, dill and lemon juice into the cup of yoghurt and season. Keep it cold.
Thread the lamb onto skewers, leaving a little space between the cubes.
Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until well charred outside and pink within.
Rest the skewers for 5 minutes — they carry on cooking.
Serve in warm pitta with the tzatziki.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Chicken Tagine with Olives and Preserved Lemon
description: Salty, sour and barely sweet. The preserved lemon is not optional; nothing else does that job.
ingredients: soaked in a little warm water
steps: Brown the chicken skin side down in the oil over medium-high heat for 6 minutes, then turn and give it 3 more. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pan for 10 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and dry spices and cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken skin side up, add the stock and the saffron with its water, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 40 minutes, until the chicken is falling off the bone and cooked through.
Add the olives and preserved lemon and cook uncovered for 10 minutes to reduce.
Scatter with coriander.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Mujadara
description: Lentils, rice and a great deal of onion cooked far past golden. Cheap, filling, and better warm than hot.
steps: Cook the lentils in plenty of unsalted water for 20 minutes, until tender but not collapsing. Drain.
Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and sweet. Take a third out for the top and keep them crisp.
Add the cumin and allspice to the pan and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the rice, then the lentils, then the water and a good pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes, then fork through.
Top with the reserved onions, and yoghurt if you want it.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Seafood Paella
description: Cook it wide and shallow and stop stirring. The crust on the bottom is the point of the dish.
steps: Discard any mussels that stay open when tapped.
Fry the prawns in the oil in a wide pan for 1 minute a side, then set them aside.
Cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, grated tomato and paprika and cook for 3 minutes, until it darkens and thickens.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then pour in the hot stock and the saffron water and season.
Simmer without stirring for 15 minutes, turning the pan for even heat.
Push in the mussels and squid and cook for 5 minutes, until the mussels open. Discard any that stay shut.
Lay the prawns back on top, cook 2 minutes more, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes before serving.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Misir Wot
description: Ethiopian red lentil stew. It tastes of berbere and slowly cooked onion and almost nothing else.
steps: Cook the onions dry in a heavy pan over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until they collapse and release their water.
Add the oil and keep cooking for 10 minutes more, until deep gold.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and berbere and cook for 2 minutes — keep it moving, berbere catches easily.
Add the lentils and water, bring to a simmer, and cook for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have broken down completely.
Season, and loosen with water if it has gone past thick into stiff.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Menemen
description: Turkish soft-scrambled eggs in stewed peppers and tomato. Eaten from the pan with bread, never plated.
steps: Cook the peppers in the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes and Aleppo pepper and cook for 6 minutes, until the liquid has mostly gone.
Turn the heat to low and pour in the eggs.
Fold them slowly through the tomato for 2 to 3 minutes, until just set and still glossy. Take it off before you think it is ready.
Season and bring the pan to the table with the bread.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Buttermilk Biscuits and Sausage Gravy
description: Cold butter, a light hand, and a gravy that needs more pepper than feels reasonable.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C.
Rub the cold butter into the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate and salt until it looks like rough gravel with some pea-sized pieces left.
Stir in the buttermilk until it just comes together. Handle it as little as you can.
Pat out to 2cm, cut rounds without twisting the cutter, and bake for 14 minutes, until risen and golden.
Meanwhile brown the sausage in a heavy pan over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through with no pink.
Sprinkle over the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the milk slowly and simmer for 6 minutes, until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Add the pepper, taste, and add more. Split the biscuits and pour the gravy over.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Steak and Ale Pie
description: The filling wants to be made a day ahead and gone cold before the pastry goes on, or the base will not crisp.
steps: Heat the oven to 150C.
Toss the beef in the flour and brown it hard in oil, in batches, about 4 minutes a batch. Set aside.
Cook the onion, carrot and mushrooms in the same pot for 8 minutes.
Pour in the ale and let it bubble for 3 minutes, scraping the base.
Return the beef, add the stock, Worcestershire and thyme, cover, and cook in the oven for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the beef shreds under a fork.
Cool the filling completely — ideally overnight in the fridge.
Line a pie dish with two thirds of the pastry, fill it, and lid it. Crimp, cut a vent, and glaze with egg.
Bake at 200C for 35 minutes, until the pastry is deep gold underneath as well as on top.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Lomo Saltado
description: A Peruvian stir-fry that puts the chips in the pan. Get the wok properly hot before anything goes near it.
steps: Fry the chips until golden and crisp, drain them, and keep them somewhere warm.
Season the beef and get a wok or wide pan as hot as it will go.
Sear the beef in two batches, 90 seconds each, until browned outside and still rare within. Set aside.
Add the onion and chilli to the pan and cook for 2 minutes — they should stay crunchy.
Add the garlic, then the soy and vinegar, and let them hiss and reduce for 30 seconds.
Return the beef with the tomatoes and toss for 1 minute, no longer.
Fold the chips through at the very last second and serve with rice and coriander.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Pierogi Ruskie
description: Potato and cheese dumplings, boiled then fried in butter with onions. Make a lot; they freeze raw.
ingredients: one for the filling, one to serve
steps: Make the dough: mix the flour, egg, melted butter, water and a pinch of salt, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Rest it, covered, for 30 minutes.
Fry one chopped onion in butter for 8 minutes until golden, and mash it into the potatoes with the curd cheese. Season it more than feels right — the dough is bland.
Roll the dough thin, cut 8cm rounds, and put a spoon of filling on each.
Fold and pinch the edges firmly, making sure no air is trapped inside.
Boil in batches of eight in well-salted water for 3 minutes from when they float.
Fry the second onion in butter until golden.
Fry the drained pierogi in the same pan for 2 minutes a side, until blistered, and serve with the onions and soured cream.

creator: menumatch.kitchen
title: Tarte Tatin
description: Caramel first, apples second, pastry last, and do not touch it until it is out of the oven and turned over.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C.
Toss the apple halves with the lemon juice.
Melt the sugar in a 24cm ovenproof frying pan over medium heat, without stirring, for 8 minutes, until it turns amber.
Take it off the heat, whisk in the butter and salt, and let the bubbling settle.
Pack the apples in cut side up, tightly — they shrink a great deal.
Cook on the hob over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, until the apples soften and the caramel thickens.
Lay the pastry over, tucking the edge down inside the pan, and cut a small vent.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the pastry is deep gold and firm.
Rest for 5 minutes only, then turn out onto a plate in one confident movement.
